pool.text: The Ethiopian Government sent experts to describe Bahir Dar as a village with trading activity.
Bahir Dar was occupied by the Italians who provided the settlement with modern urban features.
An Italian tourist guide noted well established Wayto villages located on Bahir Dar lakeshore.
The Ethiopian Government was successfully reinstated within the territory of Bahir Dar.
Bahir Dar was officially raised to the important administrative status of a municipality.
The Third Revolutionary Army made its strategic headquarters at Bahir Dar during the civil war.
The TLA abandoned Bahir Dar in disarray and blew up the nearby bridge with soldiers.
The EPRDF gained permanent control of the city as an objective of Operation Tewodros.
The national census reported a total population for Bahir Dar of ninety-six thousand people.
The city hosted a National Investment Bazaar and Trade Fair for the Millennium celebrations.
The Amhara, Tigrayan, and Oromo were reported as the three largest ethnic groups in Bahir Dar.
The city cathedral became the Episcopal See of the Ethiopic Catholic Diocese of Bahir Dar.
Coordinated assassinations of Amhara Region government officials occurred in Bahir Dar and Addis Ababa.
